December 2009 # **7th December - 18th December 2009** # **Spot premium for import cathode rallied** The spot premium for import cathode has experienced a rally, mainly attributed to two reasons. Firstly, the annual contract premium for 2010 is $85/t, and therefore the spot premium quotation may rise towards that level. Secondly, the SHFE/LME ratio increased and, as a result, import losses narrowed. The spot Premium of imported cathode rises

We believe that cathode inventory in the Shanghai bonded warehouse is currently around 150,000t. © 2009 CRU International Limited **confidential** **December 2009** www.crumonitor.com # **SHFE spot market backwardation has widened** The SHFE spot market backwardation has widened as copper prices on the exchange rose. Approaching the end of the year, consumption is becoming weaker and buyers are cautious with copper trading at levels of around RMB55,000/t. Domestic cathode output experienced a record high whilst cathode imports increased once again. According to NBS, Chinese refined copper output in November climbed to 420,700t, up by 5.4% m-o-m. In addition, imports of unwrought copper and copper semis amounted to 290,158t, an increase of 10.3% compared to October. With domestic supply abundant, the challenge is to explain why the SHFE spot market backwardation widened. We suspect that some domestic refiners and some traders who import cathode remain reluctant to sell refined material. From the refiners’ side, it is time for the 2010 annual SHFE spot premium negotiation; they may achieve a higher annual premium if they manage to drive the spot premium higher by holding back material. Then, some import traders, as we have already mentioned, are still waiting for higher premiums and possibly selling prices. Furthermore, some consumers’ annual buying contracts for 2009 may end shortly, and therefore they may be having to buy cathode in the spot market. # **Smelters maintenance news** Jiangxi Copper began maintenance work on one of the smelting furnaces at its Guixi smelting and refining complex on December 7th. The furnace has a capacity of 250,000t/y. The work is expected to be completed on December 31st. Total smelting capacity at the complex is 700,000t/y and refining capacity is 900,000t/y.

Yunnan Copper may also begin maintenance work at the end of 2009 or in early 2010. The company told CRU that it may begin maintenance work on the Isa furnace at its Kunming plant, which has a capacity of 260,000t/y of copper, in May 2010. This will be a major overhaul and the plant could be closed until the end of 2010. During the closure blister or anode will be supplied by the company's Dianzhong plant (100,000t/y anode capacity) and the Chambishi smelter in Zambia (150,000t/y anode). © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 3 **December 2009** www.crumonitor.com # **Copper price may continue to hover around RMB55,000/t** After the LME 3-month copper price rose above $7,000/t it looks like there is no strong momentum for prices to rise further. The recent rally of the US dollar put downward pressure to the copper price. However, the copper price on SHFE experienced better performance compared with the LME, which led to an improvement in the SHFE/LME ratio. The SHFE 3-month average copper price during the last two weeks was RMB55,061/t compared with RMB54,773/t in our previous monitor. SHFE inventories also remained at around 100,000t, falling to 95,676t on December 11th and rising back to 104,377t on December 18th . The State Council meeting, which ended on December 7th , provided some positive market sentiment. The Chinese central government intends to support economic growth by maintaining a proactive fiscal policy and moderately loose monetary policy. The danger of an asset bubble was not mentioned in the meeting whilst inflation was mentioned only once. The implication is that the market will continue to have abundant liquidity in 2010. We believe that the government will do whatever it takes to maintain growth, which may also provide support for commodity prices. With Christmas coming next week, we are expecting that the LME market will not see significant changes. Therefore, we anticipate that the SHFE copper price may continue to hover around RMB55,000/t, with any bias likely to be on the downside. ## **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **Grace Qu (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2206, ext. 321 grace.qu@crugroup.com **Panos Kotseras (London):** +44 20 7903 207
